summary.name: IndieWeb
summary.one_liner: IndieWeb is a community-driven movement for people-focused personal websites that own their domain, publish on their own site first, and keep control of their content.
use_cases: Owning your own domain as your online identity
Publishing articles and status posts on your own website first
Syndicating posts to other platforms while keeping them on your site
Finding meetups and events for personal website builders
Joining a community for building personal websites
summary.what_it_does: The page describes the IndieWeb as a community of independent and personal websites built on owning your domain, publishing on your own site first (optionally elsewhere), and owning your content. It says posts can be distributed to other platforms and that replies and likes from other services can be pulled back to your site. It promotes permanent, readable links and lists community activities: Homebrew Website Club meetups, IndieWebCamp gatherings, online Pop-Ups, monthly blog carnivals, and a #indieweb chat. It is a community and set of principles rather than a single downloadable product, and the page does not describe specific software in detail.
notable: Community of personal websites built on owning your domain and content
Homebrew Website Club regular meetups and IndieWebCamp gatherings
Translations in many languages and a weekly newsletter
caveats: You do not need a website to join, but you should be interested in personal websites
Page describes a community and principles rather than a specific software product
Sponsorship and donations are requested via Open Collective and swag purchases
